item.title: Cameroon is mourning the deaths of 20 Members of Parliament from the 10th Legislature.
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded: An editorial must do something different. It must ask what ceremony often avoids: what happens to democratic governance when a legislature loses not just numbers, but its institutional memory? Parliaments do not function on votes alone. They run on experience on lawmakers who understand procedure, command trust across party lines, and know when to assert power and when to restrain it. The loss of 20 legislators is therefore not only personal or regional. It is structural. Three of these losses reveal that cost with particular clarity. Hon. Dongo Essomba Jean Bernard, Member of Parliament for Lekie East in the Centre Region, served as Chief Whip of the CPDM Parliamentary Group. In any legislature, the chief whip is the unseen architect of order—coordinating votes, enforcing discipline, translating party intent into legislative outcome. Remove that role abruptly and the chamber does not collapse; it stutters. Coordination frays. Predictability weakens. Lawmaking becomes louder, slower, and less certain. Hon. Koa Mfegue Laurentine Epse Mbede, Member of Parliament for Mefou and Afamba, was the Eldest Member of the 10th Legislature. By long-standing parliamentary tradition, she presided over the opening of the March sessions, chairing proceedings until the election of the new Bureau of the National Assembly. This was not pageantry. It was guardianship of calm, procedure, and continuity at Parliament’s most delicate moment of self-renewal. Her passing removes a stabilizing anchor that cannot be restored by appointment. Hon. Abbe Michael Ndra, Member of Parliament for Donga-Mantung West (Ako/Misaje Special Constituency) in the North West Region, served on the Committee on Budget and Finance. Committees are where power is examined rather than proclaimed. Budget work is technical, slow, and unforgiving of inexperience. Losing a practiced hand there weakens oversight in ways that rarely make headlines but always shape outcomes. Yet to focus only on these three would miss the larger truth. Each of the 20 lawmakers represented a constituency now missing its advocate, a network of trust severed mid-sentence, files left unfinished. Replacement mechanisms will fill seats. They always do. But representation is relational, not mechanical. Trust is not sworn in with an oath. This moment demands institutional honesty. Are lawmakers adequately supported in health and workload? Is parliamentary memory preserved beyond individuals? Can committees and caucuses absorb sudden loss without losing rigor? Democracies rarely fail in dramatic fashion. They erode quietly through attrition, through gaps left unexamined. Cameroon’s Parliament will continue to meet. Bills will be tabled. Votes will be counted. The harder test is whether the institution can remember what it has lost and adapt without diminishing itself. In Memoriam: The 20 Members of Parliament of the 10th Legislature Centre Region * Hon. Abomo Fama Marguerite Celestine — Upper Sanaga * Hon. Dongo Essomba Jean Bernard — Lekie East * Hon. Ngaba Zogo Salomé — Lekie East * Hon. Koa Mfegue Laurentine Epse Mbede — Mefou and Afamba North Region * Hon. Ali Mamouda — Benue West * Hon. Fadimatou Samba — Mayo-Rey * Hon. Harouna Abdoulaye — Mayo-Louti Far North Region * Hon. Djibrilla Kaou — Mayo-Tsanaga * Hon. Manamourou Silikam Isabelle — Mayo-Danay * Hon. Saraou Bernadette — Mayo-Kani * Hon. Yakouba Yaya — Mayo-Sava Adamawa Region * Hon. Memouna Mahamat — Mayo-Banyo * Hon. Yaouba Alhadji — Vina Littoral Region * Hon. Ngahane Isaac — Wouri East * Hon. Ngo Yetna Marinette — Sanaga-Maritime East Region * Hon. Ngbanbaye Antoinette — Lom-et-Djerem * Hon. Tak Bienvenue — Lom-et-Djerem * Hon. Prince Mikody Ange Gilbert — Boumba-et-Ngoko South West Region * Hon. Monjowa Lifaka Emilia — Fako West North West Region * Hon. Abbe Michael Ndra — Donga-Mantung West (Ako/Misaje Special) Democracies endure not by denying loss, but by learning from it.
item.excerpt:encoded: The country has observed the rituals tributes, moments of silence, official condolences.

item.title: Privacy Policy
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
Who we are

Suggested text: Our website address is: https://theeagleseyemedia.com.

Comments

Suggested text: When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

Media

Suggested text: If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Cookies

Suggested text: If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Embedded content from other websites

Suggested text: Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Who we share your data with

Suggested text: If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.

How long we retain your data

Suggested text: If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

Suggested text: If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

Where your data is sent

Comprehensive Media Coverage

Your trusted source for parliamentary news and insights.
[elementor-element k="d6aa2fbc87054470c4fd519b8b51a68a" data=""]

What We Offer

Delivering reliable news and insights on Cameroon Parliament.
[elementor-element k="d6aa2fbc87054470c4fd519b8b51a68a" data=""]

Parliamentary Coverage

We provide detailed reports on plenary sessions, committee meetings, and legislative activities, ensuring you stay informed on all parliamentary developments.
[elementor-element k="d6aa2fbc87054470c4fd519b8b51a68a" data=""]

Legislative Insights

Our analysis of legislative actions and decisions offers valuable context, helping you understand the implications of parliamentary discussions on the public.
[elementor-element k="d6aa2fbc87054470c4fd519b8b51a68a" data=""]

Multimedia Features

We produce videos, podcasts, and articles that explore the nuances of parliamentary proceedings, making complex information accessible and engaging.
[elementor-element k="d6aa2fbc87054470c4fd519b8b51a68a" data=""]

Constituent Engagement

We highlight the activities of elected representatives and their interactions with constituents, emphasizing accountability and community involvement in governance.

Stay Updated on Parliament

Join us for the latest news and insights.
Explore Now

Contact Us

Reach out for information or assistance.

Email

Send us an email and we will get back to you as soon as possible.
[elementor-element k="d6aa2fbc87054470c4fd519b8b51a68a" data=""]

Phone

Give us a call during business hours to speak with our team.
[elementor-element k="d6aa2fbc87054470c4fd519b8b51a68a" data=""]

Office

Visit our office for a consultation or to discuss your goals.

item.title: THE EAGLE’S EYE AWARD
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
Most Active Committee – Cameroon National Assembly (2025)

Foreign Affairs Committee

Chaired by Hon. Banmi Emmanuel

The Foreign Affairs Committee of the Cameroon National Assembly, under the stewardship of Honourable Banmi Emmanuel, is hereby recognized as the Most Active Committee of the Year 2025 for its outstanding contribution to parliamentary diplomacy, legislative scrutiny, and international engagement.

Throughout the 2025 parliamentary year, the Committee distinguished itself as a vital interface between the Cameroon National Assembly and the international community. It demonstrated exceptional consistency in examining international agreements, treaties, and cooperation frameworks, ensuring that Cameroon’s foreign engagements aligned with national interests and constitutional requirements. The Committee’s work significantly enriched plenary deliberations and strengthened Parliament’s oversight role in matters of foreign policy and international cooperation.

Under the leadership of Hon. Banmi Emmanuel, the Committee also played a central role in parliamentary diplomacy, receiving foreign delegations, engaging ambassadors and international partners, and supporting the activities of parliamentary friendship groups. Its disciplined sittings, high attendance rate, and quality reports reflected strong leadership, inclusiveness, and technical rigor.

By projecting Cameroon’s parliamentary voice beyond national borders while safeguarding legislative integrity at home, the Foreign Affairs Committee reaffirmed its strategic importance within the Cameroon National Assembly, meriting recognition as the Most Active Committee of 2025.

item.title: 2026 New Year Wishes Ceremony:
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
National Assembly Closes Ranks

The Cameroon National Assembly on Tuesday hosted its traditional 2026 New Year Wishes Ceremony, a solemn institutional ritual that brought together Members of Parliament, parliamentary staff, and security personnel in a renewed spirit of unity and service to the Republic.
As scheduled on the official programme, proceedings effectively began at 10:00 a.m. with the arrival of the Senior Deputy Speaker, Hilarion Etong, who represented the Right Honourable Speaker, Cavaye Yeguie Djibril. By the time of his arrival, guests were already seated in the Banquet Hall of the National Assembly Complex, which hosted the ceremony for the second consecutive year.
Parliamentary Bureau and MPs Lead the Ceremony


The New Year wishes formally commenced with members of the Bureau of the National Assembly, who filed past to extend the symbolic greetings: “Happy New Year, Mr. Speaker.”
The delegation was led by Baoro Théophile, Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly.
They were followed by Members of the CPDM Parliamentary Group, led by Roger Melingui, Chief Whip of the group. The sequence continued with Members of Parliament from opposition parties, led by Cabral Libii, President of the PCRN political party.
The parliamentary phase concluded with the participation of National Assembly staff, underscoring the inclusive and institutional character of the ceremony.
Administration, Services and Security Units Take Center Stage
Among the first staff delegations to extend New Year wishes was the Cabinet of the Speaker, led by El Hadj Boukar Abdourahim, Chief of Staff to the Speaker.
This was followed by the General Secretariat of the National Assembly, headed by Essian Andre Noël, Secretary General.
The Questor’s Services, led by SALI, Controller General of Administration and Finance, then took their turn.

Also represented were the Parliamentary Institute of Yaounde and the Hôtel des Députés, reflecting the broad institutional ecosystem that supports parliamentary work.

A particularly striking moment came with the participation of the military and security units serving at the National Assembly. Leading this category was the Speaker’s security team, commanded by Ibrahim Yeguie Djibril, followed by the security team of the National Assembly Complex under Haman.

Honouring Merit and Service

The 2026 New Year Wishes Ceremony concluded with the award of medals of different grades to selected meritorious staff, in recognition of dedication, professionalism, and loyal service to the institution.
Beyond its ceremonial significance, the event reaffirmed the National Assembly’s commitment to discipline, continuity, and collective responsibility as Parliament enters the new legislative year, united in purpose and service to the Cameroonian people.

item.title: Hon. Agho Oliver Bamenju
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
2025 Cameroon’s Most Impactful MP on the International Stage

By all objective measures, Hon. Agho Oliver Bamenju.Member of Parliament representing Mezam North (Bafut/Tubah) constituency of the North West Region of Cameroon has emerged as Cameroon’s most influential parliamentary voice on the global stage, redefining legislative diplomacy through sustained leadership, strategic engagement, and high-level representation across continents by The Eagle’s Eye Media.

Since his election as Member of Parliament of the Republic of Cameroon on 22 March 2020, Hon. Bamenju has built an exceptional international profile, positioning Cameroon at the heart of critical global conversations on Governance, food systems, sustainable development, climate governance, cybercrime, digital rights, international justice, and democratic accountability.

His stature was further consolidated in January 2025, when he was elected Central Africa Regional Coordinator of the Africa Food Systems Parliamentary Network (AFSPaN) during the African Union Extraordinary Summit on CAADP in Kampala, Uganda a strategic role that places him at the core of continental agricultural policy coordination. Barely months later, in April 2025, he was elected 2nd Vice Chair of the Bureau of the 11th Session of the African Regional Forum on Sustainable Development, reinforcing his leadership credentials within Africa’s sustainable development architecture.

On the global rule-of-law front, Hon. Bamenju was elected Executive Committee Member of Parliamentarians for Global Action (PGA) during its 45th Annual Forum in Islamabad, Pakistan (October 2024) a testament to his credibility among lawmakers shaping international justice system .

Beyond elections, his record of active participation and keynote interventions is unmatched. From New York to Nice, Kyoto to London, Kigali to Dakar, to Abuja, to Nairobi to Kampala, to Abuja, to Abidjan,to Rabat,to Gaborone, to Bonn, to Strasbourg, to New York, to Washington, to Bucharest,to Hague, Hon. Bamenju has consistently represented Cameroon at UN High-Level Political Forums, Ocean Conferences, Internet Governance Forums, Cybercrime Conventions, Climate Change Summits, and Food Systems Platforms. Notably, he delivered an official statement on behalf of Parliamentarians for Global Action at the United Nations Ocean Conference in France, amplifying global parliamentary voice within the UN system.

Equally remarkable is his footprint in digital governance and cyber policy, with engagements at ICANN High-Level Government Meetings, Council of Europe cybercrime sessions in Strasbourg, and multiple African and global forums on AI, electronic evidence, and digital rights. His role in  enabling Cameroon to become a state party to the  Budapest Convention on Cybercrime stands as a landmark contribution to national and international legal alignment. 

Hon. Bamenju’s influence also extends to election observation and democratic governance, having served as a short-term international elections observer in the United Kingdom and the Netherlands, while contributing to parliamentary capacity-building initiatives across Africa, Europe, Asia, and North America.

His extensive membership and executive roles spanning PGA, APNIG, AFSPaN, CPA, IMF World Bank Parliamentary Network, Climate and Circular Economy networks, and global youth parliamentary platforms underscore a rare blend of continuity, relevance, and cross-sectoral expertise.

In an era where parliamentary diplomacy shapes global outcomes, Hon. Agho Oliver Bamenju stands out not merely for presence, but for impact. His trajectory reflects a disciplined commitment to projecting Cameroon as a serious, informed, strong, United, Resilient and influential global player and partner  in international policymaking.

Measured by leadership roles, consistency, scope, and substance, Hon. Agho Oliver Bamenju is today Cameroon’s most impactful Member of Parliament on the international stage.

item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
Hon. Awutah Donates Medical Equipment Worth FCFA 10.8 Million to Andek Health Centre

The Member of Parliament for Momo West Constituency in the North West Region, Hon. Awutah Philip Atubah, has donated medical equipment valued at FCFA 10,800,000 to the Andek Medicalised Health Centre in Ngie Sub-Division, further strengthening healthcare delivery in the area.

The donation was officially handed over on behalf of the lawmaker by the 1st Deputy Mayor of Ngie Council, Mr. Chekoh John, to the Medical Officer in charge of the Andek Medicalised Health Centre, during a brief but symbolic ceremony.

The medical equipment, intended to improve the quality of care and enhance the operational capacity of the health facility, comes at a time when rural health centres continue to face increasing demand amid limited resources.

Receiving the equipment, the Medical Officer expressed profound gratitude to Hon. Awutah Philip Atubah, describing the gesture as timely and impactful. The health official noted that the donation will significantly boost service delivery and improve patient care for the population of Andek and neighbouring communities.

Notably, this donation is not the first of its kind by the Momo West lawmaker to the Andek Medicalised Health Centre. In 2023, Hon. Awutah Philip Atubah similarly donated medical equipment worth FCFA 7 million to the same facility, underscoring his sustained commitment to improving healthcare services at the grassroots level.

This consistent support reflects Hon. Awutah Philip Atubah’s dedication to the wellbeing of his constituents and his broader vision of strengthening public health infrastructure across Momo West. Health personnel and community members have once again commended the initiative as a testament to responsive, people-centred leadership.

item.title: Veteran Parliamentarian Hon. Laurentine Koa Mfegue, Spouse Mbede, Passes Away
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
Cameroon’s parliamentary community is in mourning following the death of Honourable Laurentine Koa Mfegue, spouse Mbede, Member of Parliament for the Mefou-et-Afamba Constituency, who passed away on 22 January 2026 in Yaoundé.

The information was confirmed by family sources.

Her absence during the recent ceremony for the presentation of New Year wishes to the President of the Republic at the Paul Biya Glass Palace had been observed, though no official concern had been raised at the time. According to persons close to the late Honourable Member, she remained in regular telephone communication until recent days.

Hon. Laurentine Koa Mfegue, spouse Mbede, last took part in parliamentary proceedings in December 2025, during plenary sittings held shortly after the official visit of women parliamentarians to the newly appointed first female Prosecutor General at the Supreme Court of Cameroon.

A longstanding militant of the Cameroon People’s Democratic Movement (CPDM/RDPC), she began her political career within the Soa Municipal Council before being elected Mayor of the Soa Council in 2002. She entered the National Assembly during the Ninth Legislature in June 2012, where she served as an active member of the Committee on Foreign Affairs until 2024.

On 10 March 2020, during the opening of the statutory parliamentary session, she was conferred the honorary distinction of Dean by Age, in accordance with parliamentary tradition.

Beyond her legislative responsibilities, Honourable Koa Mfegue distinguished herself through sustained advocacy for the promotion of women in public life. Through the Democracy in the Feminine initiative, she encouraged greater female participation in governance and civic leadership nationwide.

In March 2024, her address at the opening of the first ordinary parliamentary session of the year drew significant attention, as she openly called on Members of Parliament to uphold discipline, accountability, and institutional commitment.

Renowned for her frank parliamentary language, moral authority, and loyalty to republican institutions, the late Honourable Member leaves behind the legacy of a devoted legislator whose service contributed meaningfully to Cameroon’s democratic life.

Tributes continue to emerge from political stakeholders, parliamentary colleagues, and constituents of Mefou-et-Afamba, as the nation reflects on the loss of a respected figure of legislative history.

item.title: Honourable. Etombi Gladys ikome Hosts Saker Baptist College Ex-Students
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
The National Assembly of Cameroon on Thursday opened its doors to a delegation of over 200 ex-students of Saker Baptist College, Limbe, in a landmark civic and educational visit marked by strong parliamentary symbolism and institutional engagement.

At the heart of the visit was Honourable Etombi Gladys Ikome, Member of Parliament for the Fako East Constituency of the South West Region, who joined her fellow Ama Mata in celebrating the legacy of the renowned academic institution while strengthening the bridge between Parliament and citizens.

The delegation was received at the Paul Biya Glass House, the new parliamentary complex that stands as a symbol of modern governance, transparency and democratic maturity.

For Honourable Etombi Gladys Ikome, the visit carried deep personal and national significance blending her role as a legislator with her identity as a proud product of Saker Baptist College, an institution credited with moulding generations of disciplined women leaders.

item.title: Hon. Malomba Donald Chairs South West PIB Review, Flags Accountability Gaps in Manyu
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
Honourable Malomba Donald, Member of Parliament representing the Buea Urban Constituency, has reaffirmed the imperative of transparency and accountability in the management of public funds as he chaired the second-semester review of the 2025 Public Investment Budget (PIB) for the South West Region.

The high-level session of the Regional Participatory Committee, held on Thursday, 22 January 2026, brought together a broad spectrum of stakeholders, including elected officials of Regional and Local Authorities, representatives of public administrations, civil society organisations, traditional rulers, project contractors, and members of the media.

At the centre of deliberations was a critical assessment of how effectively public investments delivered tangible impact for communities across the South West Region during the 2025 financial year.

Speaking during the review, Hon. Malomba Donald underscored that while notable progress was recorded in some project sites driven by transparency, supervision, and institutional diligence serious concerns were equally raised over implementation lapses in certain areas.

Particular attention was drawn to Manyu Division, where the committee identified worrying gaps in project execution, monitoring, and delivery timelines. These shortcomings, participants agreed, undermine public confidence and weaken the developmental purpose of the Public Investment Budget.

“Accountability remains non-negotiable,” the Buea Urban lawmaker stressed, insisting that public resources must be managed with the highest sense of responsibility and measurable impact.

The participatory review provided a platform for frank exchanges, enabling stakeholders to jointly acknowledge successes while openly confronting deficiencies. The process, observers noted, reflects Parliament’s growing emphasis on results-based governance and citizen-centred development.

Hon. Malomba further reiterated that public investments must translate into real benefits for the population, stressing that every franc allocated under the PIB must work for the people it is intended to serve.

In line with inclusive governance principles, the parliamentarian encouraged citizens, development actors, and community leaders to remain engaged in the oversight process, calling for continued dialogue and feedback to strengthen future budget execution.

The Regional Participatory Committee review forms part of Cameroon’s broader framework aimed at improving fiscal transparency, enhancing local development outcomes, and reinforcing accountability in the decentralised management of public funds.

As the 2026 budget cycle unfolds, stakeholders say the lessons drawn from the 2025 review will be crucial in ensuring that public investment projects across the South West Region deliver sustainable and equitable development.

item.title: Organising Committee for APF 51st General Assembly Officially Installed in Yaoundé
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
January 22, 2026 Cameroon has officially launched preparations for the hosting of the 51st General Assembly of the Parliamentary Assembly of La Francophonie (APF) with the formal installation of the event’s Organising Committee.

The installation ceremony was held on Wednesday at the banquet hall of the Paul Biya Glass House, headquarters of the National Assembly, under the chairmanship of the Senior Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly, Hon. Hilarion Etong. He is also President of the APF Cameroon Branch and the current President of the Parliamentary Assembly of La Francophonie.

The General Assembly is scheduled to take place in Yaoundé from July 7 to 12, 2026, and is expected to welcome over 400 parliamentarians and delegates from the four major regions of the Francophone world.

Ceremony Highlights

Proceedings began at 12:15 p.m. with the arrival of the presiding authority. The opening segment featured a video presentation outlining the mandate of the APF, its parliamentary activities, and the facilities of the National Assembly that will be used during the upcoming international meeting.

This was followed by the reading of the Presidential Order establishing the Organising Committee, presented by Mr. John Mamong, Technical Adviser at the National Assembly and Administrative Secretary of the APF Cameroon Branch.

During the presentation, the composition of the Organising Committee was unveiled, including 15 specialised sub-committees entrusted with the day-to-day planning and coordination of the General Assembly.

Call for Commitment and Excellence

In his installation address, Hon. Hilarion Etong emphasised the significance of the event for Cameroon’s parliamentary diplomacy and international image.

He urged members of the Organising Committee to demonstrate professionalism, unity, and dedication in order to ensure a successful hosting that will bring honour to the country and strengthen the standing of Cameroon’s parliamentary institutions.

At the close of his address, he officially declared the members of the Organising Committee installed on behalf of the Right Honourable Speaker of the National Assembly and the President of the Senate.

Operational Roadmaps Unveiled

The final phase of the ceremony focused on the presentation of operational roadmaps to guide the work of the various sub-committees. The presentation was delivered by Mr. Bouba Halidou, Consultant, who outlined the strategic framework for effective coordination and timely execution of assigned responsibilities.

Concluding the ceremony, the President of the APF reaffirmed that the general coordination team, under his leadership, remains open to proposals and innovative ideas capable of strengthening the organisation of the 51st General Assembly.

He also expressed appreciation to the Speaker of the National Assembly, Right Honourable Cavaye Yeguié Djibril, for his decisive role in enabling Cameroon to host this major parliamentary event of La Francophonie.

The ceremony ended at 1:20 p.m., officially marking the start of Cameroon’s final preparations ahead of the July 2026 APF General Assembly in Yaoundé.

item.title: Hon. Njume Peter Ambang’s Parliamentary Network Emerges Cameroon’s Most Impactful of 2025
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
In a year marked by pressing public health challenges and rising expectations for legislative leadership, Hon. Njume Peter Ambang has distinguished himself as the architect of Cameroon’s most active, results-driven and influential parliamentary network of 2025.

Through the Parliamentary Caucus on Health Financing, which he founded and continues to lead, Hon. Ambang has transformed parliamentary advocacy from routine oversight into a powerful engine for national health reform. The caucus has become the most visible and coordinated parliamentary platform in the country, linking lawmakers directly with government, development partners, and international institutions.

Unlike conventional parliamentary groupings, the caucus under Hon. Ambang’s leadership has delivered measurable outcomes — increased health budget allocations, strengthened domestic financing, renewed donor confidence, and concrete investments in malaria elimination.

Its impact reached the highest level of government when sustained parliamentary lobbying led to the creation of the Multisectoral Committee for Health by the Prime Minister, a rare institutional bridge bringing together ministers, Parliament, civil society, the private sector and global partners.

By every metric — influence, outcomes, international recognition and lives impacted — Hon. Njume Peter Ambang’s parliamentary network stands as Cameroon’s best and most active parliamentary network of the year 2025.

item.title: Hon. Njume Peter Ambang: Redefining Parliamentary Leadership Through Health Financing Advocacy
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
At a time when health financing remains one of Africa’s greatest development challenges, Hon. Njume Peter Ambang has emerged as one of Cameroon’s strongest legislative voices pushing for sustainable solutions.

As founder of the Parliamentary Caucus on Health Financing, the Member of Parliament has consistently argued that healthcare should not be treated as expenditure, but as national investment.

His approach blends policy knowledge, budgetary engagement and strategic diplomacy — ensuring Parliament does not merely debate health issues but actively shapes funding outcomes.

Through sustained engagement with the Ministries of Finance, Public Health and the Economy, Hon. Ambang has succeeded in repositioning health financing at the centre of national priorities, setting a new benchmark for issue-based parliamentary leadership.

item.title: Hon. Mbongnyor Naomi Backs Ndu Peace Talks
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
In a renewed push to restore harmony and social cohesion in Ndu Subdivision, the Ndu Council has convened an inclusive peace dialogue that brought together traditional, religious, political, and community stakeholders from across the municipality.

The peace talks, organized at the invitation of the Mayor of Ndu Council, El Hadji Abdou Kanfon Borno, witnessed the active participation of Honourable Mbongnyor Naomi Ngando, Member of Parliament for the Ndu Constituency, alongside a broad spectrum of local actors committed to rebuilding peace.

The high-level gathering brought together representatives of all active forces within the municipality, cutting across ethnic, religious, and social lines. Among those in attendance were 11 Fons, seven Ardos, youth leaders from both farming and grazing communities, Christian pastors, Muslim imams, sub-chiefs from major quarters of Ndu, as well as elites drawn from different parts of the country.

Held in a calm yet emotionally charged atmosphere, the meeting provided a rare platform for open dialogue. Participants spoke candidly about the pain and exhaustion caused by prolonged insecurity, including recurring killings, kidnappings for ransom, and persistent theft that have continued to undermine peaceful coexistence in the subdivision.

In a unified voice, stakeholders declared their collective rejection of violence, stressing that the population of Ndu is weary of bloodshed and yearns for stability, security, and normalcy. Calls were repeatedly made for an immediate cessation of violence and the restoration of lasting peace.

After extensive working sessions, participants unanimously resolved to set aside differences and collaborate across communities to give peace a genuine chance. Concrete commitments were made by traditional authorities, religious leaders, youth representatives, and political actors to serve as ambassadors of dialogue within their respective communities.

To ensure sustainability of the resolutions reached, the Ndu Council announced that follow-up actions and peace-building mechanisms will be coordinated through the Peace, Justice and Reconciliation Initiative, an institutional framework created by the council to promote long-term stability and community healing.

Speaking through their actions and consensus, participants left the meeting with renewed hope that Ndu Subdivision long known as a peace-loving community can reclaim its tradition of coexistence and mutual respect.

The presence of Hon. Mbongnyor Naomi Ngando at the peace talks was widely welcomed, reinforcing the importance of parliamentary support in grassroots peace-building efforts and underlining the shared responsibility of elected officials and local authorities in safeguarding social harmony.

As Ndu continues its journey toward reconciliation, stakeholders expressed optimism that the dialogue marks a turning point  a new beginning anchored on unity, justice, and enduring peace.

item.title: Three Bamusso Villages Get Pipe-Borne Water Thanks to Hon. Ngalle Etongo
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
In a decisive demonstration of responsive leadership and people-centered governance, the Member of Parliament for Bamusso Constituency, Hon. Ngalle Daniel Etongo, has successfully delivered pipe-borne water to three communities in his subdivision  Betika, Bekumu, and Boa Balondo  addressing one of the most urgent social needs of the population.

The water projects were officially unveiled during the Parliamentarian’s grassroots tour of villages across the Bamusso Subdivision, a mission that combined development action with political mobilization ahead of the forthcoming twin elections.

Widely described by constituents as an ever-present, dynamic and pragmatic legislator, Hon. Ngalle Daniel Etongo once again translated representation into tangible impact, reinforcing his reputation as a lawmaker whose interventions align directly with the daily realities of his people.

Development with Purpose

Access to clean and safe drinking water has long remained a critical challenge in many rural communities of Bamusso. By extending pipe-borne water to Betika, Bekumu and Boa Balondo, the MP has not only improved public health conditions but also strengthened community resilience and dignity.

Residents who spoke to The Eagle’s Eye Media expressed profound appreciation, noting that since his election into the National Assembly, Hon. Ngalle Daniel Etongo has consistently responded to the exact priorities of the constituency, rather than symbolic gestures.

“He understands our problems and acts. That is leadership,” a community elder remarked.

Political Mobilization Ahead of Twin Elections

Beyond development, the parliamentary tour served as a strategic civic engagement platform. During interactive meetings with militants and community stakeholders, the MP  who also serves as Section President of the CPDM strongly encouraged party faithful to massively register on ELECAM electoral registers, underscoring the importance of civic participation.

He further briefed militants on the national stakes of the upcoming elections, calling for unity, discipline, and unwavering loyalty to the ideals of the ruling party.

Unshakable Support for the CPDM Leadership

Across the three villages, constituents reaffirmed their total and unflinching support for:

  • President Paul Biya, National Chairman of the CPDM, and
  • Hon. Ngalle Daniel Etongo, whom they described as their illustrious son and dependable representative.

Community voices echoed a common message: confidence, serenity, and readiness as the nation prepares for the electoral calendar.

A Model of Constituency Representation

With this latest intervention, Hon. Ngalle Daniel Etongo continues to embody the principle that parliamentary mandate must be felt at grassroots level where legislation meets livelihood.

As anticipation builds toward the twin elections, his blend of development delivery, political clarity, and grassroots presence positions Bamusso as a constituency firmly aligned with progress, stability, and continuity.

item.title: Hon.Etombi Gladys Hosts Saker Baptist College Ex-Students
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
The National Assembly of Cameroon on Thursday opened its doors to a delegation of over 200 ex-students of Saker Baptist College, Limbe, in a landmark civic and educational visit marked by strong parliamentary symbolism and institutional engagement.

At the heart of the visit was Honourable Etombi Gladys Ikome, Member of Parliament for the Fako East Constituency of the South West Region, who joined her fellow Ama Mata in celebrating the legacy of the renowned academic institution while strengthening the bridge between Parliament and citizens.

The delegation was received at the Paul Biya Glass House, the new parliamentary complex that stands as a symbol of modern governance, transparency and democratic maturity.

For Honourable Etombi Gladys Ikome, the visit carried deep personal and national significance blending her role as a legislator with her identity as a proud product of Saker Baptist College, an institution credited with moulding generations of disciplined women leaders.

Proceedings began with a formal protocol session, during which the President General of the Saker Baptist College Ex-Students Association, Madam Nkeng Magdalene, delivered a goodwill message highlighting the school’s enduring contribution to women’s education and national development.

The delegation was officially welcomed by the Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly, Honourable Mary Muyali Meboka, personal representative of the Right Honourable Cavaye Yeguie Djibril, Speaker of the National Assembly.

In her address, the Deputy Speaker provided a detailed overview of the evolution of the National Assembly as a republican institution and traced the vision behind the construction of the Paul Biya Glass House, describing it as a modern architectural expression of legislative authority and national unity.

Following the presentations, the visitors undertook a guided tour of the three main components of the National Assembly Complex  the General Secretariat, the Plenary Hall, and the Banquet Hall.

The tour offered participants first-hand exposure to the legislative environment where national laws are debated, adopted and promulgated, while reinforcing public understanding of parliamentary procedure.

Throughout the visit, Honourable Etombi Gladys Ikome remained actively engaged with members of the delegation, facilitating exchanges and encouraging greater citizen participation in democratic life.

A major highlight of the event was the cutting of an anniversary cake commemorating the 64th anniversary of Saker Baptist College, a moment that underscored the institution’s rich heritage and its continuing relevance in nation-building.

Honourable Etombi was assisted during the visit by Honourable Datouo Theodore and the Second Deputy Secretary General of the National Assembly, Mr. Martin Sakwe Elangwe, whose coordination ensured the smooth execution of the programme.

The visit formed part of ongoing efforts by the National Assembly to promote civic education, institutional transparency and citizen inclusion, particularly among women’s and educational organisations.

The active participation of Honourable Etombi Gladys Ikome reflected Parliament’s commitment to nurturing informed citizenship and reaffirmed the vital role of education in shaping responsible leadership.

As the delegation departed the Glass House, the visit stood as a symbolic reminder that democratic institutions draw their strength not only from lawmaking, but from sustained engagement with the people they serve.

item.title: Hon. Mbongnyor Naomi Ngando Takes Development to the Doorsteps
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
The Member of Parliament for the Ndu Constituency Honourable Mbongnyor Naomi Ngando, has continued to assert a strong presence at the grassroots through a series of development oriented and humanitarian interventions aimed at improving living conditions and strengthening traditional institutions within the municipality.

On Wednesday, January 28, the lawmaker donated 100 bags of cement to support the renovation of the Mbipgo Fon’s Palace. 

The handover ceremony took place in the presence of the Development Chairperson, traditional notables and community leaders.

Receiving the consignment, the Fon of Mbipgo expressed appreciation for what he described as a timely and meaningful gesture. He assured that the materials would be put to effective use for the ongoing rehabilitation works, while commending the parliamentarian for promoting politics that delivers visible development to the people.

The traditional authority further recalled that at the beginning of her mandate, Hon. Mbongnyor Naomi Ngando had supported the Mbipgo Health Centre with ten hospital mattresses and a generator, a contribution that improved the operational capacity of the facility.

In furtherance of her community development drive, the Member of Parliament also provided a consignment of wheelbarrows, spades and digging forks to the village of Sina, intended to support routine maintenance of community roads. 

 The equipment was handed to village representatives to facilitate collective road works and ease movement, particularly during the rainy season.

Barely a day later, on Thursday, January 29, the MP extended similar support to the Ndu Fon’s Palace, donating another 100 bags of cement for the ongoing facelift of the traditional institution.

While receiving the materials, the Fon of Ndu described the donation as timely, noting that it came at a critical stage of renovation works. He offered prayers and blessings for the parliamentarian, encouraging her to continue serving the population with dedication and commitment.

The recent donations form part of a broader pattern of sustained engagement with traditional authorities across the municipality. 

Over the years, Hon. Mbongnyor Naomi Ngando has supported renovation works at several palaces, including Ngulu, Nseh Makop, Wowo, Boyar Sub-Palace, and other sub-palaces in Mbipgo. In line with custom, she has also consistently donated a cow to nearly all palaces during Bfubfu cultural celebrations, reinforcing cultural heritage and community cohesion.

Beyond infrastructure and tradition, the lawmaker has also demonstrated solidarity in times of crisis. Following the January 14 armed attack in Gidado, Mbandfung, Hon. Mbongnyor Naomi Ngando on January 29 donated 20 bags of rice to survivors of the attack.

The humanitarian assistance was handed over in Gidado, where beneficiaries expressed gratitude and called for lasting peace in the conflict-affected area. Many noted that the gesture brought relief at a moment of deep trauma, while renewing hope that stability would soon return to the region.

Through these successive interventions, Hon. Mbongnyor Naomi Ngando continues to reinforce a model of parliamentary representation grounded in proximity, solidarity and practical development reflecting a leadership approach that places community welfare at the centre of public service.

item.title: When a Legislature Loses Its Memory
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
Cameroon is mourning the deaths of 20 Members of Parliament from the 10th Legislature. The country has observed the rituals tributes, moments of silence, official condolences. An editorial must do something different. It must ask what ceremony often avoids: what happens to democratic governance when a legislature loses not just numbers, but its institutional memory?

Parliaments do not function on votes alone. They run on experience on lawmakers who understand procedure, command trust across party lines, and know when to assert power and when to restrain it. The loss of 20 legislators is therefore not only personal or regional. It is structural.

Three of these losses reveal that cost with particular clarity.

Hon. Dongo Essomba Jean Bernard, Member of Parliament for Lekie East in the Centre Region, served as Chief Whip of the CPDM Parliamentary Group. In any legislature, the chief whip is the unseen architect of order—coordinating votes, enforcing discipline, translating party intent into legislative outcome. Remove that role abruptly and the chamber does not collapse; it stutters. Coordination frays. Predictability weakens. Lawmaking becomes louder, slower, and less certain.

Hon. Koa Mfegue Laurentine Epse Mbede, Member of Parliament for Mefou and Afamba, was the Eldest Member of the 10th Legislature. By long-standing parliamentary tradition, she presided over the opening of the March sessions, chairing proceedings until the election of the new Bureau of the National Assembly. This was not pageantry. It was guardianship of calm, procedure, and continuity at Parliament’s most delicate moment of self-renewal. Her passing removes a stabilizing anchor that cannot be restored by appointment.

Hon. Abbe Michael Ndra, Member of Parliament for Donga-Mantung West (Ako/Misaje Special Constituency) in the North West Region, served on the Committee on Budget and Finance. Committees are where power is examined rather than proclaimed. Budget work is technical, slow, and unforgiving of inexperience. Losing a practiced hand there weakens oversight in ways that rarely make headlines but always shape outcomes.

Yet to focus only on these three would miss the larger truth. Each of the 20 lawmakers represented a constituency now missing its advocate, a network of trust severed mid-sentence, files left unfinished. Replacement mechanisms will fill seats. They always do. But representation is relational, not mechanical. Trust is not sworn in with an oath.

This moment demands institutional honesty. Are lawmakers adequately supported in health and workload? Is parliamentary memory preserved beyond individuals? Can committees and caucuses absorb sudden loss without losing rigor? Democracies rarely fail in dramatic fashion. They erode quietly through attrition, through gaps left unexamined.

Cameroon’s Parliament will continue to meet. Bills will be tabled. Votes will be counted. The harder test is whether the institution can remember what it has lost and adapt without diminishing itself.

In Memoriam: The 20 Members of Parliament of the 10th Legislature

Centre Region

  • Hon. Abomo Fama Marguerite Celestine — Upper Sanaga
  • Hon. Dongo Essomba Jean Bernard — Lekie East
  • Hon. Ngaba Zogo Salomé — Lekie East
  • Hon. Koa Mfegue Laurentine Epse Mbede — Mefou and Afamba

North Region

  • Hon. Ali Mamouda — Benue West
  • Hon. Fadimatou Samba — Mayo-Rey
  • Hon. Harouna Abdoulaye — Mayo-Louti

Far North Region

  • Hon. Djibrilla Kaou — Mayo-Tsanaga
  • Hon. Manamourou Silikam Isabelle — Mayo-Danay
  • Hon. Saraou Bernadette — Mayo-Kani
  • Hon. Yakouba Yaya — Mayo-Sava

Adamawa Region

  • Hon. Memouna Mahamat — Mayo-Banyo
  • Hon. Yaouba Alhadji — Vina

Littoral Region

  • Hon. Ngahane Isaac — Wouri East
  • Hon. Ngo Yetna Marinette — Sanaga-Maritime

East Region

  • Hon. Ngbanbaye Antoinette — Lom-et-Djerem
  • Hon. Tak Bienvenue — Lom-et-Djerem
  • Hon. Prince Mikody Ange Gilbert — Boumba-et-Ngoko

South West Region

  • Hon. Monjowa Lifaka Emilia — Fako West

North West Region

  • Hon. Abbe Michael Ndra — Donga-Mantung West (Ako/Misaje Special)

Democracies endure not by denying loss, but by learning from it.

item.title: new year wishes
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
Hon.Yeba Judith Receives Grassfields Community of mfoundi VI

The Tennis Club of the Hôtel des Députés last Saturday the 31st of January provided a dignified setting for a warm New Year wishes ceremony in honour of Judith Yeba Sama, bringing together sons and daughters of the Grassfields community of Yaoundé VI in a vibrant display of tradition, solidarity, and gratitude.

Clad in traditional attire befitting the occasion, community members converged in a spirit of fellowship to celebrate a leader they described as attentive, committed, and deeply connected to the grassroots. The ceremony, rich in cultural symbolism, underscored the enduring bond between the Honourable and the people she serves.

Delivering the keynote address, Mrs. Lucienne Zounou Ketchouozo, President of the Grassfields Association of Yaoundé VI, paid glowing tribute to Hon. Judith Yeba Sama’s steadfast engagement alongside local populations. Speaking with visible emotion, she conveyed heartfelt appreciation and affection, wishing the legislator continued success and divine guidance in the year ahead. Her remarks, marked by sincerity, drew sustained applause from the gathering.

In her response before the traditional exchange of greetings, Hon. Judith Yeba Sama expressed profound gratitude for the show of unity. “This is truly touching,” she said. “To witness such solidarity and love among us fills my heart with joy.” She commended the leadership and dedication of the Grassfields Association of Yaoundé VI, describing its members as a constant source of inspiration.

The Honourable went on to acknowledge her family, friends, neighbours, and a broad spectrum of women’s groups whose presence amplified the ceremony’s significance. Among those recognised were women from the North-West Region, the Balikumbat Humble Ladies, the Joyful Sisters, and the Femmes Dynamiques of Etoug-Ebe. “You are all incredible women,” she remarked. 

“May the Almighty reward you a hundredfold. Thank you, and Happy New Year to all.”

The event was further elevated by the attendance of friends and well-wishers from across Yaoundé, as well as Prudencia Injoh Foo Ngang Awa, her parliamentary colleague of the 10th Legislature, whose presence highlighted the collegial spirit within the National Assembly.

Beyond the formalities, the ceremony stood as a powerful reminder of the role community solidarity plays in public life affirming that leadership, when rooted in shared values and mutual respect, continues to draw strength from the people it represents.

item.title: Parliament Steps Into the Digital Classroom
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
At the invitation of Professor Nalova Lyonga Pauline, Cameroon’s Minister of Secondary Education, members of the National Assembly Committee on Education, Professional Training and Youth paid a working visit to Government Bilingual High School (GBHS) Essos, Yaoundé. 

The visit offered lawmakers a first-hand appraisal of how digital learning reforms are being implemented across the secondary education sub-sector.

The parliamentary delegation was led by Hon. Gabriel Fandja, Chairperson of the Committee, alongside Hon. Njume Peter Ambang, Deputy Chairperson, and committee members Hon. Manjuh Nestus and Hon. Evina Ovambe Bernadette.

During the on-site demonstrations, officials from the Ministry of Secondary Education walked the legislators through smart classrooms, connected learning platforms, and digital tools currently deployed at GBHS Essos. Muluh Godson, a digital education expert at the ministry, underscored the transformative role of cloud computing and artificial intelligence in equipping “third-generation learners” with skills aligned to a fast-evolving, technology-driven world.

Addressing the visiting MPs, Minister Nalova Lyonga expressed appreciation for the committee’s presence and engagement, emphasizing the importance of legislative oversight in consolidating reforms. She reaffirmed her commitment to sustained collaboration with Parliament, noting that a shared vision and coordinated action are essential to building a future-ready education system.

In his remarks, Hon. Gabriel Fandja commended the minister’s initiative to open classrooms to lawmakers, describing the visit as timely and instructive.

Addressing the visiting MPs, Minister Nalova Lyonga expressed appreciation for the committee’s presence and engagement, emphasizing the importance of legislative oversight in consolidating reforms. She reaffirmed her commitment to sustained collaboration with Parliament, noting that a shared vision and coordinated action are essential to building a future-ready education system.

In his remarks, Hon. Gabriel Fandja commended the minister’s initiative to open classrooms to lawmakers, describing the visit as timely and instructive.

 He pledged the committee’s readiness to “do the needful” to ensure the ministry is adequately supported to enhance quality education nationwide.

Echoing these sentiments, Hon. Njume Peter Ambang praised the minister’s innovative drive, crediting ongoing reforms with reshaping secondary education delivery in Cameroon. 

He noted that witnessing the reforms in practice strengthened the committee’s resolve to back policies and resources that expand digital access and learning outcomes.

The GBHS Essos visit stands as a practical bridge between policy and practice aligning ministerial reform, parliamentary oversight, and classroom realities in Cameroon’s push toward a digitally empowered education system.

item.title: Hon. Injoh Projects Cameroon’s Nuclear Security Leadership at PGA Africa
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
Cameroon has reaffirmed its growing commitment to nuclear and radiological security at the PGA Regional African Cluster Workshop on Engaging Female Parliamentarians in Promoting Nuclear and Radiological Security, held in Dar-es-Salaam, Tanzania, from 23–24 February 2026. The country’s position was articulated in a comprehensive paper presented by Honourable Injoh Foo Ngang Prodencia Awa, Member of Parliament, under the theme “Nuclear and Radiological Security in Cameroon.”

In her presentation, Hon. Injoh outlined Cameroon’s geopolitical and institutional context, noting that the country is a member of the Economic and Monetary Community of Central African States (CEMAC). Bordered by Nigeria, Chad, the Central African Republic, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, and the Republic of Congo, and with its capital in Yaoundé, Cameroon has a population of approximately 31 million people and operates bilingually in English and French alongside more than 250 indigenous languages. 

She stressed that while Cameroon does not possess nuclear power plants or research reactors, it manages nearly 200 radioactive sources used in medicine, research, and other civilian applications.

Central to Cameroon’s nuclear governance architecture is the Radiological Safety and Nuclear Security Authority (ASRAN), formerly known as the National Radiation Protection Agency. 

The regulatory body, placed under the Ministry of Scientific Research and Innovation led by Dr. Madeleine Tchuinte, oversees radiation safety and nuclear security nationwide. Hon. Injoh highlighted Decree No. 2024/599 of 19 November 2024, which reorganized and strengthened the authority’s mandate, ensuring strict lifecycle control of radioactive sources, licensing of users, criminalization of related offences, and implementation of Law No. 2019/012 on radiological and nuclear safety.

The Cameroonian legislator underscored the country’s adherence to key international legal instruments, including the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons, the Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material and its amendment, and the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty, for which Cameroon hosts a monitoring station.

She noted that although Cameroon has not yet ratified the International Convention for the Suppression of Acts of Nuclear Terrorism, Parliament through the support of the Parliamentarians for Global Action (PGA) is actively encouraging government action toward ratification.

On physical protection and material control, Cameroon continues to operate a secure storage facility for low-activity disused radioactive sources, inaugurated in 2019 with international support. 

The facility centralizes and safeguards spent sources against unauthorized access. ASRAN maintains an updated national inventory of ionizing radiation sources and conducts inspections, import-export controls, and searches for orphan sources to mitigate risks associated with theft or illicit trafficking.

International cooperation remains a cornerstone of Cameroon’s nuclear security strategy. 

The country collaborates closely with the International Atomic Energy Agency and the National Nuclear Security Administration of the United States. Through these partnerships, Cameroon implemented a Nuclear Security Support Plan and received tailored assistance during the 2021 Africa Cup of Nations to enhance radiological protection measures.

A new Country Programme Framework for 2024–2029 signed with the IAEA prioritizes nuclear and radiological safety and security among its strategic areas.

A significant focus of the workshop was the role of women in advancing nuclear governance.

Hon. Injoh emphasized that Cameroonian women are increasingly active in regulatory compliance, radiation protection, public awareness, and scientific research. Engagement is bolstered through initiatives such as Women in Nuclear Africa, Women in Nuclear Global, and the Women in Nuclear Security Initiative, alongside Canadian-funded parliamentary projects between 2023 and 2025 aimed at promoting ratification and implementation of core nuclear security conventions.

 She also cited national awareness seminars organized in March 2025 in collaboration with the United States Nuclear Regulatory Commission to strengthen public communication and technical capacity.

Despite these achievements, Cameroon faces notable challenges, including internal security tensions, porous borders, and busy maritime corridors that heighten risks of illicit trafficking. Hon. Injoh called for enhanced parliamentary oversight, sustained funding, and broader public outreach to consolidate legislative backing and reinforce operational readiness.

Concluding her address, the Cameroonian MP affirmed that while the country has laid a solid legal and institutional foundation for nuclear and radiological security, continued vigilance, enforcement, and international cooperation are essential. Her intervention at the Dar-es-Salaam workshop positioned Cameroon as a proactive African state leveraging female parliamentary leadership to strengthen global nuclear security norms and safeguard public health and the environment.

item.title: Cameroon Gallops to Regional Dominance at Fombina Derby
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
Kamssouloum Abba Kabir, Member of Parliament for Logone and Chari Division in the Far North Region and 1st Quaestor of the Cameroon National Assembly, has hailed Cameroon’s resounding triumph at the prestigious Fombina Derby International Horse Racing Competition, describing it as a defining moment for the nation’s sporting prestige and cultural diplomacy.

Speaking at a press conference convened at the Hôtel des Députés in Yaoundé in his capacity as President of the Cameroon Federation of Equestrian Sports, Hon. Kamssouloum outlined the strategic groundwork that propelled the national delegation to an outstanding performance in Yola, Adamawa State, Federal Republic of Nigeria. 

He stressed that the competition was not merely a sporting engagement, but a patriotic mission that showcased Cameroon’s rising influence in sub-regional equestrian sports.

Held from January 28 to 31 in Yola, the annual derby brought together elite riders and equestrian teams from across the Lake Chad Basin. Competing against seasoned regional contenders, Cameroon emerged as one of the most decorated delegations, clinching an impressive 15 medals four gold, five silver, and six bronze  a feat that drew admiration from observers and stakeholders alike.

According to Hon. Kamssouloum, the remarkable medal haul was the result of months of rigorous preparation, structured training, and seamless coordination between riders, trainers, and technical staff. 

 He commended the athletes for their discipline, resilience, and professionalism, noting that their performance reflected both technical excellence and national pride.

Hosted in Yola, the derby is widely regarded as one of the most prestigious horse racing festivals in the region. Beyond the thrill of competition, it celebrates the deep-rooted traditions of horsemanship shared by communities across northern Cameroon and northeastern Nigeria, reinforcing historical ties and cultural solidarity.

Hon. Kamssouloum emphasized that Cameroon’s success at the derby not only strengthens the country’s international sporting reputation but also preserves and promotes a vital aspect of cultural identity in the Far North Region. He highlighted the socio-economic importance of equestrian activities, which remain deeply embedded in the traditions and livelihoods of many communities.

Looking ahead, the federation president called for sustained investment in equestrian infrastructure, expanded youth training programs, and enhanced cross-border sporting exchanges. 

He reaffirmed his commitment to broadening opportunities for young riders and fortifying institutional partnerships to consolidate Cameroon’s leadership in the discipline.

Concluding the briefing, Hon. Kamssouloum described the 15-medal triumph as a powerful symbol of national pride, unity, and competitive excellence. He pledged that the Cameroon Federation of Equestrian Sports would continue to champion sporting distinction, cultural diplomacy, and international competitiveness in future editions of the Fombina Derby and beyond.

item.title: PROFESSOR NALOVA LYONGA Unveils Artificial Intelligence Classroom
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
The Prime Minister and Head of Government, Joseph Dion Ngute, on Tuesday, March 3th, 2026, officially inaugurated a state-of-the-art Artificial Intelligence (AI) Classroom at Lycée Général Leclerc in Yaoundé, marking a decisive step in Cameroon’s digital transformation of its education sector.

The groundbreaking project was realized under the visionary leadership of the Minister of Secondary Education, Nalova Lyonga, whose unwavering commitment to innovation continues to reshape the landscape of secondary education in the country. The AI Classroom is designed to integrate advanced digital tools, interactive smart boards, and artificial intelligence-driven learning systems into everyday teaching and learning.

The initiative was co-funded by Promethean and the Commonwealth Enterprise and Investment Council, highlighting the strength of public-private and international partnerships in advancing Cameroon’s educational modernization agenda. The collaboration ensures not only cutting-edge equipment but also sustained technical support and teacher capacity-building.

In a strong gesture of transparency and institutional accountability, Professor Nalova Lyonga invited the Committee on Education, Professional Training and Youth of the National Assembly of Cameroon to be part of the historic ceremony. The committee was represented by Hon. Njume Peter Ambang, Hon. Evina Bernadette Evambe, and Hon. Manju Nestus, reflecting parliamentary oversight and endorsement of the reform-driven initiative.

In his address, Prime Minister Chief Dr. Joseph Dion Ngute underscored the strategic importance of artificial intelligence in preparing Cameroon’s youth for the demands of a rapidly evolving global economy. He emphasized that integrating AI into secondary education is a forward-looking investment in human capital, innovation, and national competitiveness.

Education stakeholders present at the ceremony described the AI Classroom as transformative, noting that early exposure to artificial intelligence will enhance students’ critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving skills. The facility is expected to serve as a catalyst for broader digital integration across the national education system.

Professor Nalova Lyonga’s steadfastness toward innovation was widely praised during the event. 

Her reform-oriented leadership continues to prioritize quality, relevance, and technological advancement, ensuring that Cameroonian learners are not left behind in the global digital revolution.

Beyond Lycée Général Leclerc, the AI Classroom is projected to serve as a pilot model for replication in other secondary schools nationwide.

With bold leadership, strategic partnerships, and parliamentary collaboration, Cameroon is steadily positioning its education sector at the forefront of technological progress in Africa.

item.title: Cameroon National Assembly Female Staff Celebrates in Grand Style
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
Female workers of the Cameroon National Assembly joined the global community on Saturday, March 8, 2026, to commemorate International Women’s Day with a colourful and spirited celebration at the institution’s headquarters, popularly known as the Paul Biya Glass House.

After a week marked by intense preparations, sporting competitions, and humanitarian activities, the women of the legislative institution gathered in a festive atmosphere to crown their efforts with a memorable ceremony dedicated to the recognition of women’s contributions within and beyond the parliamentary environment.

The activities were championed by Fadimatou Cavaye, whose leadership and encouragement gave the celebrations a special touch. Throughout the week, the organisational process was meticulously coordinated by Awudu Mabel Epse Ndikum, who ensured that every detail of the programme was carefully executed.

The official ceremony was chaired by Muyali Mary Epse Meboka, Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly, who attended as the special representative of Madam Fadimatou Cavaye, wife of the Speaker, Cavaye Yeguie Djibril.

In her remarks during the event, the Chairperson of the Organising Committee, Madam Awudu Mabel Epse Ndikum, praised the commitment and unity demonstrated by the female staff throughout the week of activities. 

 She urged women to continue embodying responsibility, professionalism, and solidarity in both their professional duties and personal lives.

“The celebration of International Women’s Day is not only a moment of joy,” she noted, “but also an opportunity for women to reaffirm their commitment to excellence, responsibility, and service to the nation.”

The gathering reflected a strong spirit of camaraderie among the female workforce of the National Assembly, highlighting their invaluable role in supporting the smooth functioning of Cameroon’s legislative institution.

As the festivities unfolded in a lively and elegant atmosphere, the celebration served as both a tribute to women’s achievements and a renewed call for greater dedication to the values of hard work, unity, and empowerment.

The event concluded with moments of cultural display, shared reflections, and expressions of gratitude, leaving participants with a deep sense of pride in their collective contribution to the parliamentary institution and to the broader advancement of women in society.

item.title: THE EAGLE’S EYE MEDIA ANNOUNCES DAILY PUBLICATION AS PARLIAMENTARY SESSION OPENS
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
As the national political stage comes alive with the opening of the parliamentary session, The Eagle’s Eye Media has announced a special editorial initiative to provide readers with more timely, comprehensive, and authoritative coverage of parliamentary affairs.

For the next 30 days, The Eagle’s Eye will move from its regular publication rhythm to a daily edition, ensuring that readers receive up-to-date reporting, in-depth analysis, and exclusive insights from the heart of Parliament.

This exceptional editorial decision reflects the media house’s unwavering commitment to keeping citizens informed during a crucial period of legislative activity, when key national issues, debates, and institutional developments are expected to shape the political landscape.

Speaking on the initiative, Publisher Etienne Ndage noted that the daily publication will enable the outlet to deliver real-time updates and deeper parliamentary reporting, while maintaining the professionalism and credibility that have become the hallmark of The Eagle’s Eye.

“With Parliament in session, the demand for reliable and timely information becomes even greater. Our decision to publish daily for the next thirty days is a deliberate effort to bring our readers closer to the workings of Parliament and to ensure that no significant development goes unnoticed,” the publisher stated.

Renowned for its distinctive editorial voice and its motto “Eye of The Parlement,” The Eagle’s Eye has steadily positioned itself as a trusted platform for parliamentary news, institutional coverage, and governance reporting.

During the special 30-day period, readers can expect breaking parliamentary updates, exclusive interviews with lawmakers, policy analyses, and behind-the-scenes reports that illuminate the legislative process and the broader governance ecosystem.

As the parliamentary session unfolds, The Eagle’s Eye stands ready now more than ever to keep its watchful gaze firmly fixed on the nation’s democratic institutions, delivering the stories that matter most to the public.

item.title: PARLIAMENTARY DIPLOMACY
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
Cameroon Parliament Showcases Commonwealth Engagement During Open Door Day

The Cameroon National Assembly on Friday, 6 March 2026, hosted a Commonwealth Parliamentary Open Door Day, an initiative aimed at strengthening public awareness of the values, programmes and opportunities offered through the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association.

The event, organised in line with Commonwealth parliamentary traditions, was chaired by the Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly, Hon. Muyali Mary epse Meboka, who presided on behalf of the Speaker, Rt. Hon. Cavaye Yeguie Djibril, currently on an official mission to Turkey.

Held within the parliamentary precincts, the open-door initiative brought together Members of Parliament, Senators and parliamentary staff for an informative exchange highlighting the shared heritage of Commonwealth legislatures and the benefits available to member states such as Cameroon. The programme featured presentations and discussions on how parliamentarians, parliamentary staff and citizens can better leverage Commonwealth platforms in areas including governance, education, youth engagement and democratic development.

Speaking during the deliberations, Hon. Tabot Lawson Bokia, Member of Parliament for Meme and Secretary of the National Assembly Bureau, underscored the professional opportunities available through Commonwealth institutions. He noted that parliamentary staff could benefit from specialised training programmes offered by Commonwealth-affiliated universities in Ghana and Nigeria, which are designed to deepen understanding of parliamentary practice and the broader objectives of the Commonwealth.

The event also saw the participation of members of the Commonwealth parliamentary family from Cameroon’s Upper House, including Senator Otte Andrew and Senator Fon Chafah Isaac, reflecting the bicameral commitment of Cameroon’s Parliament to Commonwealth cooperation.

Addressing the press at the close of the programme, Deputy Speaker Muyali Mary epse Meboka described the open-door session as an important platform for public enlightenment on the role of the Commonwealth in parliamentary development.

She explained that the meeting served as an exchange forum intended to help citizens better understand the functioning of the Commonwealth and, in particular, the work of the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association within national legislatures.

“The objective was essentially an informative exchange so that people can better understand what the Commonwealth is about, especially as it concerns Parliament and the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association,” she stated.

The Deputy Speaker further emphasised that the Commonwealth remains a credible international organisation that has continued to support Cameroon’s democratic consolidation, particularly through initiatives that promote the rule of law, parliamentary strengthening and youth empowerment.

According to her, young Cameroonians and educational institutions are encouraged to explore the various opportunities offered through Commonwealth programmes, including training, academic exchanges and leadership development initiatives.

She added that a wealth of information on these opportunities is readily accessible through official Commonwealth platforms, urging citizens to take advantage of the benefits available to Cameroon as a member of the global association.

The Open Door Day formed part of ongoing efforts by the Cameroon Parliament to foster transparency, deepen public engagement and reinforce the country’s active participation within the Commonwealth parliamentary community.

item.title: 2026 LEGISLATIVE YEAR
item.dc:creator: theeagleseyemedia
item.content:encoded:
Cameroon Parliament Opens March 2026 Session Amid Procedural Adjustment at the National Assembly

The March 2026 Parliamentary Session of the Parliament of Cameroon officially opens today, Tuesday, 10 March 2026, in conformity with constitutional provisions governing the country’s legislative calendar.

As tradition dictates, the two chambers of Parliament will convene separately on the same day. The Cameroon National Assembly will hold its opening sitting at 11:00 a.m., while the Senate of Cameroon is expected to meet later in the afternoon.

At the National Assembly, today’s proceedings carry particular significance as Members of Parliament are expected to undertake the election and confirmation of the Bureau of the House, the governing structure responsible for steering the institution’s administrative and legislative activities.

However, this year’s opening is marked by a notable procedural challenge. Traditionally, the inaugural sitting of a new parliamentary session is presided over by the eldest Member of Parliament, who chairs the session and supervises the election of the Bureau before handing over to the duly elected Speaker. In this instance, the member who was recognised as the eldest parliamentarian is no longer alive, creating an unusual institutional circumstance for the chamber.

Consequently, the National Assembly is expected to identify and designate the next eldest members among the serving Members of Parliament to preside over the opening sitting and oversee the conduct of the Bureau elections.

The Bureau of the National Assembly is composed of the Speaker, the First Vice-Speaker, five Deputy Speakers, twelve Secretaries, and four Quaestors. The current Speaker, Cavaye Yeguie Djibril, is expected to preside over subsequent proceedings once the Bureau is formally constituted.

Following the election of the Bureau, lawmakers will proceed with the formation of the Assembly’s nine specialised oversight committees. Each committee is made up of twenty Members of Parliament and is responsible for examining draft legislation, scrutinising government action, and providing sectoral oversight in key areas of national governance.

Meanwhile, the Upper House of Parliament, the Senate of Cameroon, will convene later in the afternoon to begin its own activities for the March session.

The opening of the parliamentary session thus sets the stage for an intense period of legislative work, institutional organisation, and oversight, as both chambers of the Parliament of Cameroon resume their constitutional mandate of representing the Cameroonian people and shaping the country’s legislative agenda.
